simple.meaning: נָקֹד (nâqôd) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “spotted.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 30:32. The surrounding context includes family line, flock, righteousness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָקֹד (H5348) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: נָקֹד (nâqôd) / H5348 is traced through Genesis 30:32, Genesis 30:33, Genesis 30:35, Genesis 30:39 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: I will pass through all your flock today, removing from there every speckled and spotted one, and every black one among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats. This will be my hire.

timeline.evidenceText: I will pass through all your flock today, removing from there every speckled and spotted one, and every black one among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats. This will be my hire.
I will pass through all your flock today, removing from there every speckled and spotted one, and every black one among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats. This will be my hire.

So my righteousness will answer for me hereafter, when you come concerning my hire that is before you. Every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and black among the sheep, that might be with me, will be considered stolen.”

That day, he removed the male goats that were streaked and spotted, and all the female goats that were speckled and spotted, every one that had white in it, and all the black ones among the sheep, and gave them into the hand of his sons.
The flocks conceived before the rods, and the flocks produced streaked, speckled, and spotted.
If he said, ‘The speckled will be your wages,’ then all the flock bore speckled. If he said, ‘The streaked will be your wages,’ then all the flock bore streaked.
If he said, ‘The speckled will be your wages,’ then all the flock bore speckled. If he said, ‘The streaked will be your wages,’ then all the flock bore streaked.
During mating season, I lifted up my eyes, and saw in a dream, and behold, the male goats which leaped on the flock were streaked, speckled, and grizzled.
He said, ‘Now lift up your eyes, and behold, all the male goats which leap on the flock are streaked, speckled, and grizzled, for I have seen all that Laban does to you.

definitions.full: H5348. naqod נָקֹד adjective speckled ; — only of sheep and goats; ׳נ Gen 30:32 (twice in verse), feminine plural נְקֻדּוֺת 30:35 (all || טָלוּא ), masculine plural נְקֻדִּים 30:39 ( || id. + עֲקֻדִּים ; — all these J); masculine plural also 31:8 (twice in verse) and (+ בְּרֻדִּים עֲקֻדִּים, ) 31:10 ; 31:12 (all E).
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to mark (by puncturing or branding);
